title: uuencode.rs: Err items from scan() emit begin_offset=0 regardless of actual block position
description:
In scan_inline_uuencode(), when uuencoding::scan() yields an Err(UuError::BeginBase64) item, the handler emits InlineUUBlock { begin_offset: 0, begin_length: 0, is_encoding_problem: true }.

The ScannedBlock inside the Err path does carry position information (the UuError does not, but the iterator position is known). Setting begin_offset=0 means that for a message where the begin-base64 block appears at byte 500, the returned item falsely claims offset 0 — which may point into header content or another block entirely.

The doc says 'Always check is_encoding_problem before using this field' but callers doing range-based deduplication or UI highlighting will see a spurious offset=0 entry.

Fix: uuencoding::scan() should yield Result<ScannedBlock, (UuError, begin_offset)> — or yield Ok(ScannedBlock { is_truncated: true, ... }) with the correct offsets for all error cases including begin-base64. Alternatively the Err arm in scan_inline_uuencode() should omit begin_offset from the public struct (set to a sentinel like u32::MAX) and document that begin_offset is meaningless when is_encoding_problem=true.
